edits.quote: Bellingham Math Circle / Week 7    1 (same footer on pages 1-6)
edits.fix: Use the standard footer with the sheet id: 'Bellingham Math Circle / Week 7 / <id>' on every page.

edits.quote: Your partner plays Ben, who goes first and always takes 2 counters when he can.
edits.fix: 'Plays Ben' can be heard as 'plays against Ben' (a third player). Rewrite: 'Your partner pretends to be Ben. Ben goes first and always takes 2 counters when he can.' (Answers check: you can beat Ben from 3, 4, 6, 7 but not 2 or 5.)

edits.quote: Ring the counters taken on each turn to show every different game with 4 counters.
edits.fix: A K-1 child cannot tell whether 1,1,2 and 2,1,1 count as different games, and the answer depends on it (5 games if order matters, 3 if not; the 6-row and 9-row boards assume order matters). State once that the same takes in a different order make a different game, or have the adult say so.

edits.quote: Put a star next to each game the first player wins.
edits.fix: Children who just circled '1st' for a pile of 5 (Problem 1) may star every game. Say exactly what to mark: 'Put a star next to each game where the first player takes the last counter.' (Answer: 1,1,1,1,1 and 1,2,2 and 2,1,2 and 2,2,1.)

k-1.summary: A strong K-1 sheet: compact pile cards, correct answers throughout, and a real progression from {1,2} through a greedy opponent, changed rules, a pile of 20, and two-pile mirror games, with enough work for the whole hour. Only small fixes are needed: the footer id, the confusing 'Your partner plays Ben', and clearer wording for what counts as a different game and what to star in the enumeration problems at the end, which connect less tightly to strategy than the rest.

edits.quote: Bellingham Math Circle / Week 7    1 (same footer on pages 1-6)
edits.fix: Use the standard footer with the sheet id: 'Bellingham Math Circle / Week 7 / <id>' on every page.

edits.quote: For starting piles of 25, 30, 37, and 50 counters, would you rather go first or second?
edits.fix: The four boxes already name the piles. Shorten to 'For each starting pile below, would you rather go first or second? Explain how you know.'

grades-2-3.summary: This is the best band in the packet. It classifies {1,2} piles, tests four claimed plans against every reply (Mia and Ana win, Leo and Sam lose), classifies {1,3,4} to 20 and extends to 50, tests three more plans (Kai and Theo lose, Zoe wins), shows that {1,2,4} gives the same losing piles as {1,2}, and ends with two-pile mirror play. All answers check, the wording is plain, and it needs only the footer id and one trimmed sentence.

edits.quote: Bellingham Math Circle / Week 7    1 (same footer on pages 1-6)
edits.fix: Use the standard footer with the sheet id: 'Bellingham Math Circle / Week 7 / <id>' on every page.
Delete; the table shows the rules. Start with 'For each rule below, circle the losing piles from 1 to 24.'

edits.quote: list every winning pile from 1 to 30 where Kai's move is a mistake
edits.fix: Say what a mistake is in the W/L language just defined: 'where Kai's move leaves his partner a winning pile'. (Answer: 5, 8, 10, 12, 15, 17, 19, 22, 24, 26, 29; greedy is never wrong for 1 or 3 and for 1, 3, or 5.)

grades-4-5.summary: Mathematically rich and correct: the period-7 pattern for {1,3,4}, three hidden pairs of rules with equal losing piles, when greedy fails, reverse-engineering rules (5s: {1,2,3,4}; 0,2 mod 8: {1,4,5}; 0,3 mod 7: {1,2,6}; 0,3 mod 5 impossible), the pre-period of {1,6,9} with the pigeonhole argument, and two-pile grids leading to Sprague-Grundy labels. Only light wording fixes are needed, though the sheet is far longer than 40 minutes and the closing label definition and general periodicity proof will challenge the fourth graders.

overall.strongest: The grades 2-3 sheet tests eight named children's plans against every reply under two rules, and every answer checks.
overall.weakest: The K-1 enumeration problems (P9-P10) leave 'different game' and the star task ambiguous and drift away from strategy, and all three bands lack the sheet id in the footer.
